hiro_tonkatsu_no_kikuya.price_note: Transcribed from the shop's own printed menu card and lunch card, photographed 2026/04 and 2026/05. Prices approximate — may change.

items.ja: とんかつ定食（和豚もち豚）
items.en: Pork loin cutlet set meal, made with Mochibuta brand pork
items.note: The house default. A thick pork cutlet crumbed in panko (wheat breadcrumbs) and deep-fried, sliced and served with shredded raw cabbage. The set adds rice, tonjiru (a hearty pork-and-vegetable miso soup) and pickles. 'Mochibuta' is a branded pork prized for sweet, soft fat.

items.ja: 特上ロースかつ定食（和豚もち豚）
items.en: Premium pork loin cutlet set
items.note: Rosu = loin, the cut with the fat rim along one edge, which is where the flavour lives. 'Tokujo' means a thicker, better-marbled piece than the standard cutlet. Same rice-tonjiru-pickles set.

items.ja: ヒレかつ定食（和豚もち豚）
items.en: Pork fillet cutlet set — the leanest, most tender cut
items.note: Hire is the tenderloin: no fat, very soft, milder. The most expensive thing on the card. If you find Japanese pork fat heavy, this is the one to order.

items.ja: ジャンボチキンかつ定食
items.en: Jumbo chicken cutlet set
items.note: An oversized panko-crumbed chicken breast cutlet — the value order, and the one regulars point at when someone says they don't eat pork.

items.ja: リブロースかつ定食（限定）
items.en: Rib-loin cutlet set — limited daily quantity
items.note: 'Gentei' means they cook a fixed number a day and stop; it is gone by early afternoon on busy days. Rib-loin is the fattier, richer end of the loin.

items.en: Cutlet rice bowl — pork cutlet simmered with onion and egg over rice
items.note: The cutlet is sliced and briefly simmered in a sweet dashi-and-soy broth with onion, then set with beaten egg and slid onto rice. Softer and sweeter than the dry cutlet; comes with tonjiru and pickles.

items.en: Pork loin cutlet on its own, no rice or soup
items.note: 'Tanpin' means the plate alone — order this if you are drinking, or adding it to somebody else's set.

items.en: Premium loin cutlet, plate only
items.note: The set version of the same cutlet is ¥1,700, so the rice, tonjiru and pickles cost you ¥100 — almost everyone takes the set.

items.en: Fillet cutlet, plate only
items.note: Lean tenderloin, no fat. Eat it with the salt on the counter as well as the sauce — it shows the meat better.

items.en: Jumbo chicken cutlet, plate only
items.note: The cheapest line on the menu.

items.en: Beef tendon slow-stewed until it collapses
items.section: お昼の定食 / Lunch card side
items.note: A side dish of beef sinew simmered for hours in a sweet soy-and-miso broth until it turns to gelatin. Sticky, savoury, very good with rice or beer.

items.en: Grated daikon radish — an add-on served with the cutlets
items.section: お昼の定食 / Lunch card side
items.note: Printed on the lunch card as just 'おろし'. Grated daikon is the standard lighter alternative to thick tonkatsu sauce — cool, peppery, cuts the fried fat. It is normally served with ponzu, which contains soy sauce, so ask if that matters.

items.en: Rice, pork miso soup and pickles — what 'teishoku' adds to every cutlet
items.note: Printed under each set. Tonjiru is pork belly and root vegetables in miso — not vegetarian. A handwritten notice on the wall (2026) apologises that, because of the rice shortage and price rises, free rice refills are now limited to one per person.

hiro_tsukanto.price_note: Transcribed from the shop's own printed one-page menu, photographed 2026/07. Prices approximate — may change.

items.en: Fillet pork cutlet set
items.note: Every set here is ¥1,500 and every set comes with coleslaw, miso soup and rice — and a large rice is free, which the menu says outright. Hire is the lean tenderloin; the card asks you to pick hire or rosu.

items.en: Loin pork cutlet set
items.note: Rosu is the loin with its fat rim — juicier and more strongly porky than the fillet. Panko-crumbed, so wheat.

items.en: Fillet cutlet rice bowl set
items.note: The cutlet is sliced and simmered with onion in a sweet soy-dashi broth, bound with egg and poured over rice. Also comes as a set with coleslaw and miso soup.

items.en: Loin cutlet rice bowl set
items.note: Same bowl with the fattier loin cut.

items.en: Deep-fried horse mackerel set
items.note: Aji is horse mackerel, a small oily fish; butterflied, panko-crumbed and fried whole so the crust is thin and the flesh steams inside. The English on the shop's own menu says 'fried horse mackerel' — it is a fish, not horse.

items.ja: 鹿児島地鶏唐揚げ定食
items.en: Kagoshima free-range chicken kara-age set
items.note: Kara-age is chicken marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted in flour or potato starch and fried. 'Jidori' means a slower-grown native breed with firmer, more flavourful meat. The soy marinade means wheat regardless of the coating.

items.en: Pork liver stir-fried with garlic chives
items.note: The one non-fried set. Pork liver flash-fried with nira (garlic chives) and bean sprouts in a soy-garlic sauce — Japan's classic 'tired and need iron' dish, which is what 'jiyo' (nourishing) in the name is getting at.

items.en: Two extra pieces of fried chicken
items.section: 少しもの足りないあなたへ / For those who want a little more
items.note: Add-on, under a heading on the menu that literally reads 'for those who want a little more'.

items.en: Three panko-fried oysters
items.section: 少しもの足りないあなたへ / For those who want a little more
items.note: Hiroshima grows most of Japan's farmed oysters and kaki-furai is the local way to eat them cooked: crumbed, fried hard outside, still liquid inside. Best in the cold months.

items.ja: すべてにコールスローとお味噌汁がセットです／ご飯の大盛りは無料にて承ります
items.romaji: subete ni koorusuroo to omisoshiru ga setto desu / gohan no oomori wa muryo
items.en: Every set includes coleslaw and miso soup; a large rice costs nothing extra
items.note: Printed at the top of the card. Worth knowing before you order: there is no 'small' or 'large' set price, and asking for oomori (large rice) is free. Miso soup is made with dashi, so it is not vegan, and miso can be barley-based.

items.ja: つかんと（袋町・レモンスタンド広島内）
items.en: Lunch only, 11:30–14:00, inside another bar's premises
items.note: The shop moved on 1 July from the Nekoyacho Building to Fukuromachi 2-17, where it now runs the lunch shift inside Lemon Stand Hiroshima; from 14:00 the room becomes the lemon bar again with a completely different menu. Turn up outside 11:30–14:00 and there is no tonkatsu.

hiro_sawawa_miyajima.price_note: Read off the shop's own street A-board photographed 2025/10. Each item shows two prices: the lower is takeaway (8% tax), the higher is eat-in (10%). Prices approximate — may change.

items.en: Thick-matcha soft serve piled over warabimochi cubes
items.section: アイスクリーム / Ice cream
items.note: The flagship. 'Koicha' is the thick, syrupy grade of matcha used in tea ceremony — far more intense and more bitter than the latte grade. Warabimochi is a wobbly, translucent jelly-cake traditionally made from bracken-root starch, but shops routinely cut or replace it with sweet-potato or wheat starch, so treat it as wheat-risky unless the shop says otherwise. Contains dairy.

items.en: Thick-matcha soft serve, plain cone or cup
items.section: アイスクリーム / Ice cream
items.note: The strong version of the green soft serve — noticeably bitter, almost savoury, and the thing to order if the ordinary matcha ice cream elsewhere has tasted like nothing. Dairy-based. A cone is wheat; ask for a cup.

items.ja: お抹茶（ソフトクリーム）
items.en: Standard matcha soft serve
items.section: アイスクリーム / Ice cream
items.note: The everyday-strength green one. The board advertises Kyoto-grown, stone-milled first-flush tea. Dairy; cone is wheat, cup is not.

items.ja: ほうじ茶（ソフトクリーム）
items.en: Roasted green tea soft serve
items.section: アイスクリーム / Ice cream
items.note: Hojicha is green tea roasted over charcoal until it turns brown — nutty, toasty, almost no bitterness and no caffeine punch. The easy choice if matcha is too astringent for you.

items.ja: バニラ（ソフトクリーム）
items.en: Vanilla soft serve
items.section: アイスクリーム / Ice cream
items.note: Also sold as a mix swirl with the matcha.

items.en: Matcha warabimochi, small tub
items.note: Cool, quivering jelly squares dusted in matcha and kinako (roasted soybean flour). 'Hon-warabi' claims real bracken-root starch, the expensive kind. Eaten with a small stick, not chopsticks. Warabimochi is often extended with wheat starch, so do not treat it as gluten-free here.

items.en: Matcha warabimochi, large tub
items.note: The sharing size, sold to take back to the ferry.

items.en: Cold whisked matcha
items.note: Just powdered green tea whisked into cold water — no dairy, no grain, no sweetener. Bracing and quite bitter; the cheapest thing on the board and the most genuinely traditional.

items.en: Sweetened cold matcha drink
items.note: In Japan 'green tea' on a sweets-shop board means specifically this: matcha pre-mixed with sugar and served over ice. Sweet, mild, and not the same thing as the unsweetened 冷抹茶 above it.

items.en: Matcha latte
items.note: Matcha with milk, iced or hot. Dairy.

items.en: Roasted green tea latte
items.note: The board carried a SOLD OUT card over this one when it was photographed, so it may or may not be running.

items.en: Matcha latte with warabimochi cubes dropped in
items.note: Drink and dessert in one cup — you get a fat straw to pull the jelly cubes up through. See the warabimochi note on wheat starch.

items.en: Matcha shake — the ice cream and the latte blended together
items.note: The board explains it as matcha ice cream blended into the matcha latte, tuned sweeter and easier to drink — they pitch it at children and at people who find straight matcha too sharp.

hiro_anago_ryori_hiroshima_be.price_note: From the shop's own Gurunavi official page and its verified Tabelog menu (last updated by the shop 2021-03; Gurunavi card timestamped 2022). Tax-inclusive figures quoted. Prices approximate and now several years old — may change.

items.ja: あなごの生ちりポン酢（刺身）
items.en: Raw conger eel sashimi with ponzu — the house signature
items.note: The dish the shop is built on and the reason to come. Anago is almost never eaten raw — its blood is mildly toxic and it needs a live fish and skilled knife work — so this is rare even in Japan. The shop kills the eel the same morning, slices it thin, and serves it cold and crunchy with a strong clean sweetness. Ponzu is citrus-and-soy, so wheat.

items.en: Conger eel sashimi
items.note: The larger plate of the same raw anago. Texture is the point: springy and squeaking rather than melting like tuna.

items.en: Simmered conger eel sushi
items.note: The opposite treatment: the eel is poached until it falls apart, laid over vinegared rice and brushed with a sweet dark reduction called tsume. The shop sells it as a takeaway souvenir too. Tsume is soy-based.

items.en: Conger eel tempura
items.note: A long fillet in a thin wheat batter, fried so the flesh goes fluffy. Eat it with salt rather than the dipping broth if you want to taste the eel.

items.en: Assorted tempura plate
items.note: Anago plus whatever seasonal vegetables are in — the spring version runs to wild mountain greens (sansai).

items.ja: 海老と蓮根のはさみ揚げ
items.en: Prawn and shiso sandwiched between lotus-root slices and deep-fried
items.note: Renkon (lotus root) is the crunchy white vegetable with holes through it. Two thin discs clamp a prawn-and-perilla filling; it fries up crisp and stays juicy in the middle.

items.en: Kumamoto free-range chicken grilled over a mesh
items.note: Higodori is a Kumamoto breed. Served in the courses with a 'japonaise' sauce; ask what is on it, as most such sauces start with soy.

items.en: Raw rock oyster, summer season
items.note: Not the usual Hiroshima winter oyster. Iwagaki are a different, much bigger species that spawns in summer, so they are at their best June to August — dense, creamy, almost meaty. Raw oyster itself is gluten-free; the ponzu poured over it is not, so ask for it on the side.

items.en: Wagyu beef seared outside, raw inside, with citrus-soy
items.note: A marbled red-meat cut blasted over high heat for seconds a side, then sliced. Ponzu contains soy sauce.

items.ja: 豆腐とジャコの和風サラダ
items.romaji: tofu to jako no wafu sarada
items.en: Tofu salad with tiny dried Ondo sardines
items.note: Chirimen-jako are whitebait dried to matchstick size and scattered over like salty croutons. Ondo, on the far side of Kure, is the local source. Dressed with a soy-based wafu dressing.

items.ja: 本日のオススメ黒板メニュー
items.en: Today's blackboard specials
items.note: The shop's own page says the blackboard tracks the day's market and is deliberately priced low. If you read no other part of the menu, read this one — ask the counter to point at what came in.

items.en: Noodles in chicken broth heaped with spring onion — the closing dish
items.note: Served at the end of every course as the shime, the ritual carbohydrate that closes a Japanese drinking meal. Wheat-blended soba noodles.

items.ja: 季節の根菜　筑前煮
items.en: Root vegetables and chicken simmered in soy and dashi
items.note: A Kyushu home-cooking staple: lotus root, burdock, carrot, taro and chicken browned in oil then stewed down until glossy. Soy-based.

items.en: Spanish mackerel marinated in yuzu, soy and sake, then grilled
items.note: Yuan-yaki is a named marinade-grill technique — the yuzu peel in the marinade perfumes the fish. Sawara is a prized Seto Inland Sea fish.

items.ja: 3時間飲み放題 あなご三昧コース（全9品）
items.en: Nine-course anago blowout with three hours of unlimited drinks
items.note: The only course that includes the raw anago. Six to sixteen people, 18:00–20:30 start, phone booking only — the shop states outright that it does not take online reservations for these.

items.ja: 3時間飲み放題 ゆったり満喫コース（全8品）
items.en: Eight courses plus three hours of unlimited drinks
items.note: Includes anago sashimi but not the namachiri preparation.

items.ja: 2時間飲み放題 お得コース（全7品）
items.en: Seven courses plus two hours of unlimited drinks
items.note: The short version, aimed at groups moving on to a second bar afterwards.

hiro_sakedokoro_daijin.price_note: From the shop's own verified (公式) Tabelog menu, last updated by the shop 2026-04-08. Tax-inclusive. Prices approximate — may change.

items.en: Sea urchin and spinach fried on the teppan
items.note: A Hiroshima invention, born on the Nagarekawa drinking street in the 1970s and now on half the menus in the district. Spinach is sautéed in butter and garlic, then loosened with a paste of sea-urchin roe and sake and served bubbling in a small skillet. Rich, briny, salty; eat it fast while it steams. Ask about soy in the pan sauce.

items.en: Oyster and spinach on the teppan
items.note: The same buttery spinach treatment with Hiroshima oysters instead of urchin. Cheaper, and arguably the more local of the two.

items.en: Seared wagyu brisket-plate with citrus soy
items.note: Koune is a cut you will basically only see in Hiroshima: the fatty plate from the cow's brisket, right at the front of the ribs. Sliced thin, blowtorched, and eaten with ponzu to cut it. Deeply fatty, slightly gelatinous. Ponzu is soy-based.

items.ja: 大甚名物和牛 牛山
items.en: The house 'beef mountain' — a heap of wagyu on the griddle
items.note: Filed on the menu under 赤字覚悟, 'we know we're losing money on this'. Nami is the regular size, dai the large.

items.en: Fried Hiroshima chilli fish-cake
items.section: 揚げたて / Fried to order
items.note: Gansu is a Hiroshima thing almost unknown elsewhere: minced white fish from the Inland Sea mixed with onion and chilli, pressed flat, crumbed in panko and fried. Tastes like a spicy fish rissole; sold in every Hiroshima supermarket as a cold snack, but it is far better hot like this.

items.ja: とろける逸品 茹で豚足
items.en: Boiled pig's trotter
items.note: Simmered until the collagen goes to jelly and it can be pulled off the bone with chopsticks. Sticky rather than meaty — a classic drinker's dish, priced per trotter.

items.en: Griddled wheat noodles with brown sauce
items.note: Wheat noodles fried hard on the teppan with cabbage and pork, lacquered with the same fruity-brown okonomi sauce used on Hiroshima pancakes. Wheat in the noodles and again in the sauce.

items.en: Griddled noodles seasoned with salt instead of sauce
items.note: Lighter and more garlicky than the sauce version; you taste the noodle and the pork fat rather than the sauce. Still wheat noodles.

items.en: Cold poached chicken under Sichuan chilli-sesame sauce
items.note: 'Yodaredori' translates literally as 'drool chicken' — the Sichuan bang-bang dish. Numbing sanshō pepper, chilli oil, sesame and soy over cold chicken.

items.en: Oysters cured in oil
items.section: 早出しのアテ / Quick starters
items.note: Oysters lightly cooked then steeped in oil, often with garlic and herbs — concentrated, smoky, closer to a preserved anchovy than a fresh oyster. Many recipes start by simmering the oysters in soy; ask.

items.en: The house potato salad
items.note: Japanese potato salad is a distinct thing: potato crushed rather than cubed, bound with rice-vinegar mayonnaise, with cucumber and onion. An izakaya benchmark dish — people judge a bar by it. Contains egg.

items.en: Pickled shallots with lemon
items.section: 早出しのアテ / Quick starters
items.note: Rakkyo are small Japanese shallots pickled sweet-sour, crunchy and pungent; the lemon version is lighter. Hiroshima grows a lot of lemons, which is why they turn up everywhere here. Check the pickling liquid for soy or dashi.

items.en: Scallop in Korean-style chilli cure
items.section: 早出しのアテ / Quick starters
items.note: Chanja is normally salted cod guts fermented with gochujang; here the treatment is applied to scallop. Sharp, spicy, tiny portion, made for shōchū. Gochujang usually contains wheat.

items.en: Liver and garlic chives stir-fried
items.note: Soy-garlic sauce, high heat, done in ninety seconds on the griddle in front of you.

items.en: Wagyu offal grilled on the teppan
items.note: Horumon means the innards — intestine mostly, chewy and very fatty, which is the appeal. The name is Osaka slang from 放るもん, 'the stuff you throw away'. Usually sauced with soy or miso.

items.en: Rolled dashi omelette topped with meat
items.note: Dashimaki is egg beaten with dashi stock and rolled in layers in a rectangular pan — wet, custardy, savoury rather than sweet. The dashi is bonito-based, so not vegetarian.

items.en: Grated mountain yam griddled into a soft cake
items.note: Yamaimo grated to a slippery foam and cooked on the teppan until the outside sets and the inside stays molten. Very Hiroshima teppan-bar. Usually bound with egg and dashi and finished with sauce — ask.

items.en: 'Prawn vs oyster battle' — both griddled on one plate
items.note: The name is a joke about a duel. Butter-fried prawns on one side, oysters on the other.

items.en: Fried chicken thigh, priced per piece
items.section: 揚げたて / Fried to order
items.note: Ordered by the piece, so you can have one with a beer without committing to a plate. Soy-marinated and flour-dusted.

items.en: Fried chicken gizzard with Uyghur spice
items.section: 揚げたて / Fried to order
items.note: Sunazuri (also sunagimo) is the gizzard — dense and crunchy like a scallop that has been to the gym. The cumin-heavy Uyghur spice mix is a modern izakaya fashion.

items.en: Compulsory seating snack — but here it is all-you-can-eat
items.note: Almost every Japanese izakaya charges an otoshi cover and gives you one small dish for it. This shop's own note says theirs is refillable without limit, which is unusual and worth knowing.

items.ja: 店名変更：酒処 大甚 → 酒処 大人
items.en: The shop now trades as 酒処 大人 at the same address
items.note: Same premises at Nagarekawa-cho 1-7, relaunched 2 March 2026 under the new writing 大人; older listings and this app's record still say 大甚. Open 17:30–23:30, closed Sundays.

hiro_koryoriya_nagayama.price_note: From the shop's own website menu page (tax-inclusive) plus its verified Tabelog drinks list. Much of the counter changes with the season, so expect items to come and go. Prices approximate — may change.

items.en: Local conger eel served raw as sashimi
items.note: Anago is nearly always cooked; serving it raw needs a live fish and fast knife work, and this shop keeps it on all year, which is unusual. Faintly sweet with a springy bite. The shop calls it their most-ordered dish among regulars. Eaten with soy.

items.en: Conger eel grilled plain, with no sweet glaze
items.note: Shirayaki is the connoisseur's order: the eel is grilled naked so you taste the fish and the char instead of the sugar-and-soy tare. The shop serves it with a wasabi-mustard-salt condiment. Ask whether any soy is brushed on.

items.en: Chef's choice sashimi platter
items.note: The website lists what rotates through it: yellowtail, wild sea bream, bonito, firefly squid, local anago, bluefin tuna, squid. Fish comes up daily from the Osaka central market. Sashimi itself is gluten-free; the soy sauce beside it is not.

items.en: Chips made from year-aged Inca no Mezame potatoes
items.note: The shop's calling card, and the thing most people order first. Inca no Mezame is a small yellow-fleshed variety with a chestnut sweetness; they store it for a full year to concentrate the sugars, then fry it low and slow. Confirm the fryer oil is not shared with breaded items and that nothing is dusted on.

items.en: Senshu water aubergine, eaten raw
items.note: A speciality aubergine from Osaka's Senshu district so tender and full of water that it is torn by hand and eaten raw like a fruit — no bitterness at all. Summer only. Usually served with a soy-based dip; ask.

items.en: Round Kyoto aubergine under sweet meat-miso
items.note: Kamo-nasu is the big spherical Kyoto aubergine — dense and creamy when cooked, nothing like a long one. Topped with coarsely minced pork simmered in sweet miso. Miso may be barley-based.

items.en: Manganji sweet peppers with bonito flakes and soy
items.note: A long mild Kyoto chilli, more sweet pepper than heat, with just enough bitterness to keep you eating. Served the simplest possible way: grilled, soy, katsuobushi. Bonito means not vegetarian.

items.en: Miyazaki wagyu seared rare
items.note: Miyazaki beef has twice won Japan's national wagyu championship. Tataki means the outside is scorched hard and the middle left raw. Ask what the sauce is.

items.en: Seared wagyu from the grill section
items.note: The larger grill-section version.

items.en: Japanese Black wagyu steak
items.note: Priced from ¥3,000 and up depending on the cut of the day.

items.en: Conger eel tempura
items.note: Wheat batter, kept very thin here — the shop's line is that the coating should let the season through.

items.en: Assorted mountain-yam tempura
items.note: Yamaimo fries to a strange and excellent texture — crisp shell, sticky-fluffy centre. Wheat batter.

items.ja: 極太アスパラのバター焼き
items.en: Very thick asparagus fried in butter
items.note: The shop's own line is that asparagus is only worth eating for about two weeks a year, and this is that fortnight. Butter, so not vegan.

items.en: Blackthroat seaperch simmered in sweet soy
items.note: Nodoguro is one of the most expensive fish in Japan — oily to the point of tasting like fatty tuna, hence the nickname 'white toro'. Nitsuke means simmered in soy, mirin, sake and sugar until glossy.

items.en: Turban shell grilled in its own shell
items.note: A spiral sea snail set straight on the coals with sake and soy poured into the shell; you wind the meat out with a pick. The dark coil at the end is the liver — bitter, and the part locals actually want.

items.en: Sea bream heads and collars simmered in soy
items.note: 'Ara' is everything left after filleting — head, collar, backbone — and it is the best-eating part. Messy, cheap, and where the flavour hides.

items.en: Whole sweetfish grilled with salt
items.note: Ayu is a summer river fish eaten whole, guts and all — the bitterness of the innards against the sweet flesh is the whole point. Shioyaki means nothing but salt and fire, so no soy or wheat touches it; still confirm the grill is not shared with tare-brushed items.

items.en: Dried flatfish, lightly toasted
items.note: A Setouchi speciality: small flounder dried board-flat in the winter wind, then toasted and beaten with a mallet to loosen the flesh, which you tear off in strips. Intensely savoury, chewy, made for sake. Plain dried fish with nothing added, but ask if any soy dip comes with it.

items.en: Seared spicy cod roe
items.note: A whole sac of pollock roe cured with chilli, grilled just enough to firm the outside while the middle stays creamy. Salty enough that a mouthful lasts a whole cup of sake. The cure normally includes soy and sake.

items.en: Tiny freshwater clam soup
items.note: Ordered at the end of the night — shijimi clams are the Japanese hangover cure, and this thin miso soup full of them is what regulars finish on. Miso may be barley-based.

items.en: Roasted green tea gelato
items.note: The only dessert on the card. Dairy.

items.en: Chef's tasting course, three price levels
items.note: The ¥6,000 course runs dashi-chazuke, four appetisers, sashimi, seasonal tempura, grilled anago shirayaki and a Miyazaki wagyu dish. Unlimited drinks can be added for ¥2,500. Book by 23:00 the day before. The shop invites you to declare allergies and dislikes when booking, which is the opening you want.

items.en: Dry junmai sake from Saijo, Hiroshima's sake town
items.note: Saijo, twenty minutes east of the city, is one of Japan's three great sake districts. The shop keeps about ten sake at a time and lists each with its Sake Meter Value (+8 here means firmly dry). Junmai sake is rice, water, kōji and yeast only.

items.ja: ≪呉≫雨後の月 別誂純米吟醸
items.romaji: Ugo no Tsuki betsuatsurae junmai ginjo (Kure)
items.en: Aromatic junmai ginjo from Kure, on the coast south of the city
items.note: One of Hiroshima's most admired breweries; the name means 'the moon after rain'. Ginjo grade means the rice is polished further, giving fruit and floral aromatics. Rice-based, no wheat.

items.ja: 季の美（クラフトジン）ジントニック
items.en: Kyoto craft gin and tonic
items.section: クラフトジン / Craft gin
items.note: Ki No Bi is Kyoto's own gin, built on a rice spirit base and botanicals including yuzu, sanshō and gyokuro tea. Distilled spirits are normally fine on gluten but confirm if you are strict.

hiro_amanjaku_okonomiyaki.price_note: Transcribed from the shop's own counter menu cards and street blackboard, photographed 2026/07. Prices approximate — may change.

items.ja: お好み焼き（そば/うどん）肉玉
items.en: Hiroshima okonomiyaki with pork, egg and noodles — the default order
items.note: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is not the Osaka batter-mix pancake. It is built in layers on the griddle: a paper-thin wheat crepe, a mountain of shredded cabbage and bean sprouts, pork belly, then a nest of pan-fried noodles, then a fried egg — all flipped together and lacquered with sweet-brown okonomi sauce. 'Soba or udon' is the choice you will be asked: soba here means springy yakisoba noodles (wheat, not buckwheat), udon means fat soft wheat noodles. Wheat in the crepe, the noodles and the sauce, so there is no version of this dish without it.

items.ja: スペシャル（そば/うどん）生イカ！生エビ！豚ダブル！目玉焼き！
items.en: Loaded okonomiyaki: raw squid, raw prawn, double pork, fried egg
items.note: The everything version. 'Nama ika' and 'nama ebi' mean fresh squid and prawn cooked on the griddle rather than pre-cooked, which is the difference worth paying for.

items.ja: 焼きそば / 焼きうどん
items.en: Griddled noodles without the pancake
items.note: Same noodles, cabbage and pork, fried on the teppan and sauced, but no crepe and no egg dome. The lighter order.

items.ja: スペシャル焼きそば / 焼きうどん
items.en: Loaded griddled noodles — squid, prawn, double pork, fried egg
items.note: The noodle version of the special.

items.en: Add-ons, any one for ¥150
items.note: The card lists: 生イカ raw squid, 生エビ raw prawn, 大葉 shiso leaf, 納豆 fermented soybeans, にんにく garlic, イカ天 fried squid-tempura crisps (a Hiroshima favourite — they go soggy inside the pancake on purpose), 餅 rice cake, キムチ kimchi, チーズ cheese, 目玉焼き extra fried egg, コーン sweetcorn, 野菜ダブル double vegetables, 豚ダブル double pork.

items.en: Wagyu brisket-plate seared on the griddle
items.note: Koune is a Hiroshima-only cut: the fatty plate at the front of the cow's brisket. Sliced thin and seared hard — very rich, slightly gelatinous, the local answer to yakiniku. Ask about the dipping sauce.

items.en: Pork belly wrapped in a thin omelette
items.note: Griddle-bar staple: strips of pork belly and a few vegetables folded inside a flat egg sheet, then sauced and mayo-striped like an okonomiyaki. Sauce is wheat-based.

items.en: Offal and vegetables stir-fried on the teppan
items.note: Horumon is intestine and other innards — chewy and very fatty. Usually finished with a soy or miso sauce.

items.en: Chicken marinated in soy and ginger, dusted in potato starch and fried
items.note: Tatsuta-age differs from kara-age in the coating: pure potato starch, which fries pale and shatteringly light rather than golden and craggy. The soy marinade still means wheat.

items.en: Japanese potato salad
items.note: Crushed rather than cubed, bound with rice-vinegar mayonnaise. Contains egg.

items.en: 'We have another 40 to 50 dishes'
items.note: The street board says so in as many words — what is printed is a fraction of the range. Ask the counter. There is also a one-drink-minimum per person rule, and the shop only opens 17:00–22:00.

items.ja: 生ビール（スーパードライ）
items.en: Draft Asahi Super Dry
items.note: Beer is brewed from barley malt — never gluten-free, whatever else on the menu might be.

items.en: Suntory Torys whisky with soda
items.note: The cheap national highball. Made from a blended whisky with a malt component, so not gluten-free.

items.en: Shochu highball on tap, choose a flavour
items.note: Flavours listed: lemon, lime, Calpis, green apple, plum, peach, kyoho grape, grapefruit. 'Taru-hai' means it pours pre-mixed from a keg. Base is shochu; ask if it is the barley kind.

items.en: Shochu, barley or sweet potato
items.note: Mugi is barley and imo is sweet potato. If gluten matters, the sweet-potato one is the safer of the two — barley shochu is distilled from a gluten grain.

items.ja: 冷酒 純米 賀茂鶴
items.en: Chilled Kamotsuru junmai sake
items.note: Kamotsuru is one of the historic Saijo breweries just east of Hiroshima, and the sake President Obama was poured in 2014. Junmai means rice, water, kōji and yeast only — no added distilled alcohol and no grain other than rice.

items.en: House sake, 180ml
items.note: 'Ichi-go' is the standard 180ml measure. Brewed from rice only.

items.en: House wine by the glass, red or white
items.note: Grape-based, no grain. Some wines are fined with egg or fish products, so strict vegans should ask.

items.ja: ノンアルコールビール（アサヒドライゼロ）
items.en: Alcohol-free beer
items.note: Still made from malted barley — alcohol-free is not gluten-free.

items.en: Soft drinks
items.note: Oolong tea, tomato juice, orange juice, cola, ginger ale, Calpis (a milk-based cordial, so not vegan), soda water.
